portfolio.title: Portfolio website
portfolio.description: My personal portfolio, built with Next.js, React and TypeScript. The site is designed with inspiration from the ocean. The portfolio is also a demonstration of different AI models and what they can do. The site is largely generated by AI.
portfolio.content1: This portfolio is meant to be more than a gallery; it is a demonstration of my technical and creative abilities. It is built with Next.js, React and TypeScript for performance, type safety and a modern development experience. The whole design concept is inspired by a dive into the ocean, where the user moves deeper through the content.
portfolio.content2: To deliver that experience I implemented several custom features. A dynamic scroll-progress bar shows how far the 'dive' has gone, and the navigation updates automatically to highlight the current section. I used CSS Modules for scoped styling and created subtle animations to keep the interaction lively.
portfolio.content3: As my first major project in React, this site has been a strong learning journey. It has solidified my understanding of React Hooks, component-based architecture and the benefits of Next.js server-side rendering. The project shows I can combine technical implementation with a creative design concept.

hairplant.title: Hairplant App
hairplant.description: A cross-platform Flutter app for hair transplant journeys — now live on the App Store and Google Play. Patients track their progress, upload status photos, get expert feedback and chat directly with the clinic.
hairplant.content1:
Hairplant started as a vision to digitise and improve the customer experience throughout a hair transplant journey. The idea was an all-in-one platform where users could follow their progress, upload documentation and stay in direct contact with their clinic — all in their pocket.

The project began with extensive research and user interviews to understand the real needs. Wireframes and prototypes were then developed in close collaboration with the clinic and potential users, so the solution addressed the right problems.
hairplant.content2:
Development was built on Flutter to keep the experience consistent across Android, iOS and web. Firebase was chosen as the backend for its scalability, real-time database and built-in authentication.

One of the hardest parts was designing an intuitive upload flow for status photos, where users had to take pictures at specific points in their journey. The system had to be easy to use and still give the clinic documentation in high enough quality.
hairplant.content3:
The app also includes a notification system that reminds users to upload photos on the right days. An integrated chat gives them direct access to support, which has clearly improved customer satisfaction.

Hairplant is now live on the App Store and Google Play, with real users on both iOS and Android. The project shows I can take a product from idea to a store release — including complex user flows, notifications and clinic communication.

projects.currentWork: Hairplant is now live on the App Store and Google Play. Development continues, and a split of the features is underway. My passion for building means I always have new projects going. Explore my public repositories on GitHub, or contact me directly to hear more about private projects and current work.

internship.title: Internship project
internship.description: Development of a complete Flutter admin app with a Firebase backend for a school application. The project included a live-data dashboard, a mentor system and user management to automate administrative processes.
internship.content1: During my internship at Lighthouse Digital I was asked to build a modern admin panel for an existing school app. The core of the project was to give schools tools to manage their own data and get insight through an intuitive dashboard.
internship.content2:
The existing mobile app was built on an older version of Flutter (2.x), which made a direct extension impractical. I therefore chose to rebuild the admin panel from scratch in Flutter 3.26+. That made the solution future-proof and easier to maintain. By reusing the existing Firebase/Firestore backend I could focus on frontend development and new features.

A key challenge was implementing the data visualisations. To get the charts working correctly I had to restructure parts of the Firestore database and extend the user data model. That was a useful process in data modelling and problem-solving in a live environment.

I also built a full mentor administration system, where schools can easily approve new mentors, see their status and manage access.
internship.content3: This project was a great chance to go deep into Flutter/Dart and build an application from the ground up. It gave me a solid, practical understanding of state management, dependency handling and how a frontend app talks to a BaaS platform like Firebase. Within a 3-month internship, where the first month was spent learning Flutter, I am proud to have delivered a working solution that added real value.

exam.title: Exam project
exam.description: As my final exam project I upgraded a live website from Nuxt 2 to Nuxt 3, including a full redesign. The project showed technical depth in Vue.js and a strong understanding of UI/UX principles.
exam.content1: My final exam assignment was a technically demanding migration of a live commercial website from Nuxt 2 to Nuxt 3. The task was not only a framework upgrade, but also a complete UI/UX redesign to modernise the experience.
exam.content2:
The biggest challenge was that there was no user data or analytics for the existing site. The redesign therefore had to be based on UX heuristics, competitor analysis and web design best practices. The process involved wireframing, prototyping and user testing to validate design choices before implementation started.

The migration from Nuxt 2 to 3 was a complex job that required a deep understanding of breaking changes and the new Composition API. It was a useful process in planning and running a technical migration with minimal downtime.
exam.content3: The project was a success and was praised for both the technical implementation and the improved design. It gave me valuable experience on complex Vue.js projects and strengthened my skills in frontend architecture, UI/UX and project management.
